steps.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Create one beautifully art-directed concept sheet for a new mahjong tile collection named REMBRANDT. This is an original contemporary interpretation of Rembrandt van Rijn's OIL PAINTING: deep translucent shadow, warm directional illumination, expressive loaded brushwork, palpable impasto highlights, luminous flesh-like ochres, velvet browns and subdued vermilion. Make the painting sensuous and unmistakably painterly. Do not simply apply a sepia filter or turn everything into embossed metal. Not generic fantasy art.

Board layout: square 2048 x 2048, clean warm light stone background. Elegant restrained serif title at the top: "REMBRANDT". Small subtitle: "A · OIL & LIGHT". Six large FLAT FRONT-ON portrait tile faces in an orderly 3-column by 2-row grid, all matching 3:4 aspect ratio, subtly rounded corners. All art extends to the edges of its tile. NO physical ivory rim, no bevel, no tile thickness, no ornate picture frames, no mockup perspective. Only thin clean board gutters. Enough empty background around the board title and below each tile for small captions. Each face is its own complete miniature oil painting designed to read in a mahjong hand. Paint texture supports large legible silhouettes, without excessive fine details.

Six tiles, left to right top row then bottom row:
1. Caption below face: "1 BAMBOO · THE BIRD". One beautiful lively upright pheasant-like bird, complete body and recognisable large head in profile, chest illuminated with soft warm ivory and golden feather strokes, a deep vermilion wing and a long graceful curving tail; a deep smoky umber background. A portrait of a bird treated with the human presence and psychological intimacy of a Rembrandt portrait. The single bird must dominate the tile.
2. Caption: "3 BAMBOO · GREEN LIGHT". EXACTLY THREE thick, separately countable jointed bamboo stalk motifs: one above and two below, arranged loosely rather than ruled, each with clearly visible bamboo nodes and a couple broad leaves. All paint and all background strictly in shades of GREEN, including highlights: pale celadon and sage light on forest green and deep green-black shadows. NO beige, brown, gold, white or red anywhere in this tile. Strong pools of light and thick loaded brushstrokes provide Rembrandt-like depth within this all-green palette.
3. Caption: "5 DISKS · THE GUILD". EXACTLY FIVE broad round disks, separate with generous clear gaps, arranged quincunx: two upper, one centre, two lower. Each disk a slightly irregular painterly medallion or circular seal, luminous ochre gold, muted copper and ivory-gold glints over wine-brown and warm black ground, centre disk a little larger and warmer. Five countable circles, no extra coins or small decorative circle shapes. The feel of costly metal interpreted in heavy oil paint, not photorealistic coin CGI.
4. Caption: "8 CHARACTERS · VERMILION". The exact traditional Chinese mahjong glyphs "八" and "萬", with a large beautifully legible 八 at top and a broad dominant 萬 below, formed from rich ivory-ochre and deep vermilion impasto brushstrokes. Sweeping but accurate strokes and clear interior gaps, a few bright loaded brush marks catch the light; full-face deep burgundy-umber background. No other characters or digits.
5. Caption: "EAST · FIRST LIGHT". The exact Chinese character "東" prominently and recognisably fills the tile, large warm golden-ivory painted strokes emerging from a deep midnight brown field with restrained reddish glazed shadows. A narrow soft shaft of warm light from upper left illuminates some edges, substantial shadows between strokes. Clear correct 東 character; no landscape, scenery or other letters.
6. Caption: "RED DRAGON · THE EMBER". One enormous correct Chinese character "中" painted in deep glowing vermilion and scarlet thick oil paint, with warm orange-red highlights and mahogany shadow on a dark oxblood and umber field. Broad rectangular enclosure crossed by one long vertical stroke, TWO unmistakably open counters. A strong painterly emblem, not a literal animal or medieval crest.

Overall: sophisticated original game artwork, richly painted, dramatic but bright and readable enough to use as tile art; never tiny dull symbols lost inside black panels. Variation in light and colour across suits while clearly one family. No illustration of actual mahjong gameplay. No extra text beyond title, subtitle and the exact six captions. No watermark or artist signature.

Use case: stylized-concept.
Create one exquisite concept sheet for a new mahjong tile collection named REMBRANDT, interpreting Rembrandt van Rijn's ETCHINGS AND DRYPOINT. Expressive bitten lines, wiry spontaneous drawing, velvet burr-like black passages, energetic crosshatching, broad quiet lit spaces, warm softly textured paper. The linework must have Rembrandt's human sensitivity, not stiff decorative Victorian engraving, not generic clip-art, and not uniform computer crosshatching.

Board layout: square 2048 x 2048, clean warm light stone outer background. Restrained serif title at the top: "REMBRANDT". Small subtitle: "B · THE ETCHING ROOM". Six large FLAT FRONT-ON portrait tile faces in an orderly 3-column by 2-row grid, all matching 3:4 aspect ratio, subtly rounded corners. Each face is its own original little etching, extending to every tile edge. NO physical tile rim, bevel, thickness, ornamental borders or frames. No engraved rectangular border. No mockup perspective. Use thin generous gutters and small crisp captions below, outside the face. Artwork must be bold enough for a mahjong hand: simple dominant emblems supported by textured linework.

Six tiles, left to right top row then bottom row:
1. Caption below face: "1 BAMBOO · THE BIRD". One live upright graceful pheasant-like bird, complete recognisable head, plump chest, folded wing and long curved tail, dark sepia expressive etching on luminous pale warm paper. Feathers rendered in playful varied lines, a dark pooled shadow low on the right, feather highlights mostly unmarked paper. The whole bird strongly dominates the vertical tile. No hat or clothing.
2. Caption: "3 BAMBOO · GREEN LIGHT". EXACTLY THREE separately countable short thick jointed bamboo motifs, one above and two below, with bamboo nodes and a few broad leaves. Etched with very deep bottle-green ink on a PALE CELADON GREEN ground, selective dense green crosshatching and luminous light green unprinted areas. ALL visible colors across the whole face are strictly GREEN shades, NO ivory, beige, brown, black, gold or red. Three strong complete silhouettes and clear gaps. No extra stalks.
3. Caption: "5 DISKS · THE GUILD". EXACTLY FIVE round disks arranged quincunx: two upper, one middle, two lower. Clearly separated, full face-on round medallions with expressive concentric etched shading and a few broad graphic internal cuts, dark warm sepia ink on warm paper. The middle disk has a restrained deep rust ink accent, another has an ochre wash. No figures, no extra circular ornaments, no text inside the disks. Make all five countable at a glance.
4. Caption: "8 CHARACTERS · VERMILION". Two and only two exact traditional Chinese characters: a large "八" at the top, and a prominent "萬" below. Correct large legible strokes built with a living drypoint outline and expressive crosshatched bodies. 八 in deep sepia, 萬 in a rich muted vermilion ink accent, the warm pale parchment exposed through open spaces. Clear accurate mahjong calligraphy, not pseudo-letters. No Western numeral on tile.
5. Caption: "EAST · FIRST LIGHT". One enormous correct Chinese character "東" in deep dark sepia drypoint fills the tile; correct recognisable strokes with crisp silhouette and lively burred hatch texture. A small patch of dense background hatching behind its lower right gives strong directional light; most ground remains warm pale parchment. No landscape, extra icon, text or border.
6. Caption: "RED DRAGON · THE EMBER". One enormous correct Chinese character "中" in dark vermilion-red drypoint ink, with expressive crosshatching and selective rusty red wash. Correct broad rectangular enclosure crossed by one long vertical stroke, TWO open counters. Warm pale paper ground, faint red hatch shadows lower right. The red emblem occupies most of the face. No literal dragon creature.

Overall: scholarly yet lively, tactile, timeless; six coherent collectible print-like game faces, excellent contrast and meaningful suit color accents. Light surfaces and richly drawn dark symbols provide a distinctly different design alternative from dark oil painting. No watermarks or signatures. No other text beyond specified title, subtitle and captions.

Edit the attached Rembrandt "B · THE ETCHING ROOM" mahjong concept board. Preserve the six existing tile artworks, their 3 x 2 positions, tile dimensions and all exact titles/captions. Change ONLY the OUTER BOARD BACKGROUND: replace all transparent pixels and the damaged-looking speckled gaps around the title, captions and tile borders with a uniform opaque warm off-white stone-paper background, colour approximately #f2ecdf. Make the text clean dark brown and legible on that light background. The output must be a fully opaque flat RGB presentation sheet, with NO transparent background and NO transparency anywhere. Keep all six faces and their glyphs, the three bamboo motifs and five disks exactly as they are; this is a background repair, not an artwork redesign. Retain the exact title "REMBRANDT", subtitle "B · THE ETCHING ROOM", and all six captions.

Edit only the six captions beneath the six tiles in this existing REMBRANDT B · THE ETCHING ROOM sheet. Keep all six artworks, their positions, all colors, the fully opaque pale background, title and subtitle unchanged. Erase the full old caption under each tile and typeset these SHORT replacement captions in dark brown uppercase serif, perfectly legible and centered:
Top left exactly: "1 BAMBOO"
Top middle exactly: "3 BAMBOO"
Top right exactly: "5 DISKS"
Bottom left exactly: "8 CHARACTERS"
Bottom middle exactly: "EAST"
Bottom right exactly: "RED DRAGON"
Remove all additional words from those six caption areas, including all subtitles such as THE BIRD, REBELLION or THE GUIDE. Six simple labels only. The leading Arabic digits 1, 3, 5 and 8 MUST appear. Everything else including the existing drawings is preserved. Output fully opaque with no transparency.
